tx-denton-2026-dcad-p3-guzman-rick.name: Rick Guzman
tx-denton-2026-dcad-p3-guzman-rick.bio: Member of the Denton Central Appraisal District Board of Directors, Place 3, seeking re-election.

positions.stance: Advocates "clear and fair processes within the appraisal district, especially regarding the tax protest process."
Says he refuses to "rubber stamp approvals that favor only the taxing entities."
Would focus on "responsible oversight, open communication and accountability to Tarrant County taxpayers."
Property owners deserve an appraisal district that "follows the law, uses public funds wisely and treats every taxpayer with professionalism and respect."

tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p1-haynes-byron.name: Byron Haynes
tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p1-haynes-byron.bio: Real estate professional with 13 years of experience and more than 1,000 property valuations in Tarrant County.

positions.stance: Will push for clear, plain-language documentation of the methodology used for every valuation, including explanations on appraisal notices.
Advocates regular public reporting on board decisions, accessible open meetings, and stronger conflict-of-interest and ethics policies.
Supports auditing valuation consistency across neighborhoods and making protest processes accessible to all owners, not just those with representation.
Advocates accurate, evidence-based valuations and homestead exemption outreach, and opposes "arbitrary or politically motivated valuation increases."
Believes board members should be held to a fiduciary standard, acting in residents' best interest, and wants to expose lobbying influence on decisions.

tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p1-grissom-phyllis.name: Phyllis Durbin Grissom
tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p1-grissom-phyllis.bio: Former chair of the Delta Delta Delta executive board who has worked with school boards and superintendents on public finance and facilities planning.

positions.stance: Says TAD's job is to determine property values "fairly and accurately," neither raising values for revenue nor artificially holding them down.
"Annual appraisal does not mean annual increases. It means annual review."
Says TAD can earn trust through "accuracy, transparency, sound data and a willingness to fix what isn't working."

tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p1-syed-sayeda.name: Sayeda Bilquees Syed
tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p1-syed-sayeda.bio: Former Tarrant Appraisal Review Board member and mechanical engineer who served on the Colleyville Planning & Zoning Commission.

positions.stance: Supports "uniform and equal annual appraisals."
Supports including all properties on the tax roll.
Supports an "independent Tarrant Appraisal Review Board."
Supports an audit of the tax roll every three years.
"Follow Texas Property tax code."
Says TAD's own data show homes under $200K appraised at 106% of market value versus 71% for homes over $1M, and calls for equal appraisals.
"Property values should reflect reliable, current market information."
"Taxpayers should be treated consistently under the law."
Property owners should be able to understand how their values are determined and how major policies are made.
"Taxpayers should be able to get help navigating the appraisal and protest process."
Would focus on "responsible oversight, open communication and accountability to Tarrant County taxpayers."
Property owners deserve an appraisal district that "follows the law, uses public funds wisely and treats every taxpayer with professionalism and respect."

tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p3-adams-john.name: John Adams
tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p3-adams-john.bio: Mortgage banker for more than two decades.

positions.stance: Wants all taxpayers "simply taxed fairly and equally in proportion to any other equivalent Tarrant County property owner."

tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p3-bryant-matt.name: Matt Bryant
tx-tarrant-2026-tad-p3-bryant-matt.bio: Tarrant Appraisal District board member since 2024; former Carroll ISD trustee, semiconductor engineer and sales executive, and real estate investor.

positions.stance: Backed freezing most 2025 residential values and moving TAD from yearly to once-every-two-years reappraisals, a rule renewed this summer.
Supported requiring TAD to show more evidence before raising a home's value more than 5%.
Pushed to replace TAD's appraisal software and negotiate its price down, with the contract capped at $10 million over five years.

tx-williamson-2026-wcad-p1-hisle-piper-h.name: Hope Hisle-Piper
tx-williamson-2026-wcad-p1-hisle-piper-h.bio: Real estate professional who has helped Central Texas families buy, sell and finance homes for more than 22 years; incumbent WCAD board member.
